items.title: IDScan sued over alleged data breach affecting 153 million drivers
items.one_liner: IDScan is facing lawsuits and an FBI probe after 153M driver's license records leaked and were sold on dark-web service Nexus.
items.summary: Identity verification firm IDScan faces multiple class-action lawsuits and an active FBI investigation after a threat actor on dark-web service 'Nexus' advertised 153 million driver's license scans. The data batch reportedly includes millions of IDs, passports, and medical records scanned at car rental agencies, retailers, and financial institutions across the US and Canada. Investigative checks verified genuine user profiles in the leak, including high-profile government figures. IDScan has begun notifying corporate clients while legal firms prepare consolidated multidistrict litigation.
key_facts: Records exposed: 153M+ driver's licenses, 10M ID cards, 3M travel documents, 579K medical cards
Investigating agency: FBI New Orleans field office
items.bottom_line: A massive breach of IDScan systems exposed 153 million driver's licenses and prompted an FBI probe alongside class-action lawsuits.

claims.text: A dark-web service offered over 153 million driver's license scans allegedly stolen from IDScan.
claims.support_span: Brian Krebs originally reported on September 1 that a dark-web identity-theft service called “Nexus” advertised access to more than 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver’s license scans, 10 million ID cards, 3 million travel documents, and 579,000 medical cards.

claims.text: The FBI's New Orleans office has opened an investigation into the reported data breach.
claims.support_span: Krebs also reported that the FBI’s New Orleans office has launched an investigation into the incident, which Reuters also confirmed independently.

items.title: Proxying to Compromise: SonicWall Secure Mobile Access 0-day Exploitation
items.one_liner: Active zero-day exploitation of SonicWall VPNs requires immediate patching of SMA 1000 series appliances.
items.summary: Threat actor UTA0533 has been observed exploiting multiple zero-day vulnerabilities in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 series VPN appliances. The exploitation chain involves an authentication bypass and SSRF via the /wsproxy endpoint, leading to remote code execution and lateral movement. SonicWall released hotfixes for affected models 6210, 7210, and 8200v on July 14, 2026. Volexity's investigation revealed that compromises began as early as June 22, 2026, and involved custom malware designed specifically for these appliances.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using SonicWall SMA 1000 series must apply the July 2026 hotfixes immediately to mitigate active zero-day exploitation.

items.title: CVE-2026-0298 GlobalProtect App: Code Execution Vulnerability in Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: GlobalProtect Windows clients using SAML CBL are vulnerable to local SYSTEM code execution via PLAP input validation flaws.
items.summary: An improper input validation vulnerability exists in the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider component of the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges. The flaw affects specific version ranges of the 6.0, 6.2, and 6.3 branches on Windows when configured to use SAML authentication with the Connect Before Logon feature. Palo Alto Networks has issued updates and workaround guidance, noting no active exploitation at the time of disclosure.
items.bottom_line: Palo Alto GlobalProtect Windows users leveraging SAML with Connect Before Logon face a local SYSTEM code execution risk via MITM manipulation.

items.title: Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
items.one_liner: Astra is the first model categorized as having critical cyber capability, capable of finding zero-days and building exploits autonomously.
items.summary: Hugging Face announced that its new model, Astra, has reached the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework. This classification indicates that the model can independently identify unknown zero-day vulnerabilities and build exploits across hardened systems without human guidance. To mitigate severe misuse risks, release and development were delayed to train refusal mechanisms and introduce activity monitoring. When launched, access to Astra's high-tier cyber capabilities will initially be restricted to select testers before broadening to defensive tools like Daybreak Blue.
items.bottom_line: Astra can independently uncover and exploit zero-day flaws on hardened targets, prompting strict gated access and enhanced safeguards ahead of launch.

claims.text: Astra is the first model designated at the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under the Preparedness Framework.
claims.support_span: It is the first model we are designating at this level, and requires stronger safeguards during development and before release.

claims.text: The model achieved a 100% score on the ExploitBench benchmark evaluating exploit development from known vulnerabilities.

items.title: CVE-2026-83548: SonicWall SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances Server-Side Request Forgery Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA added an unauthenticated SSRF flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 (CVE-2026-83548) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-83548 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalogue, warning of a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) flaw in SonicWall SMA1000 appliances. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to sensitive administrative functions and execute arbitrary operations. Federal agencies are mandated under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 to apply vendor-supplied mitigations or discontinue use of affected devices by September 5, 2026.
items.bottom_line: SonicWall SMA1000 appliances face active risk from an unauthenticated SSRF vulnerability requiring immediate patching or mitigation by September 5.

items.title: Manchester Airports Group Data on 8.8 Million People Leaked After Ransom Refusal
items.one_liner: Manchester Airports Group leaks 8.8 million user records online after refusing extortion demands.
items.summary: Manchester Airports Group (MAG) suffered a data breach after the FulcrumSec extortion gang exfiltrated car park, lounge, and Fast Track booking records containing personal information for 8.8 million individuals. The attackers stated they accessed third-party hosted databases after finding administrative API keys exposed in plaintext within frontend JavaScript files across airport root domains. MAG refused a ransom demand, prompting the extortion group to leak roughly 550 gigabytes of uncompressed data, including email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations, and residential IP addresses.
items.bottom_line: Exposed administrative API keys in frontend JavaScript can lead to catastrophic enterprise database breaches and data leaks.

items.title: Thomson Reuters Court Software Breach May Have Exposed SSNs and Sealed Data
items.one_liner: Thomson Reuters C-Track court software breach exposes SSNs and sealed records across multiple U.S. states and Canada.
items.summary: Thomson Reuters disclosed that unauthorized actors accessed files from its C-Track court case management platform between March and June 2026. The breach impacted court systems across 11 U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada, potentially exposing sensitive records containing Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, dates of birth, and sealed court documents. Affected state jurisdictions and independent judicial branches, such as Minnesota, have terminated Thomson Reuters' access and are offering credit monitoring services to impacted individuals.
key_facts: Unauthorized access window: March 1 through June 29, 2026
items.bottom_line: Third-party vendor compromises in legal case management systems can expose confidential court records and Social Security numbers.

items.title: Broadcom Patches Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion VM-Escape Vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: VMware users on Windows, Linux, and macOS must update to 26H1u1 immediately to prevent guest-to-host VM escapes.
items.summary: Broadcom has released security advisory VMSA-2026-0007 to address two critical vulnerabilities in VMware Workstation and Fusion. The first, CVE-2026-59346 (CVSS 9.3), is an integer overflow in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that allows host-level code execution from a guest VM. The second, CVE-2026-59347 (CVSS 8.1), is a stack-based buffer overflow in the Host-Guest File System (HGFS) component. Both vulnerabilities affect versions 25H2 and 26H1 and have been patched in version 26H1u1.
key_facts: CVE-2026-59347: CVSS 8.1, HGFS stack-based buffer overflow
items.bottom_line: These vulnerabilities allow an attacker with local admin privileges on a guest VM to execute code on the host, effectively breaking the isolation boundary of the virtualization platform.

items.title: CVE-2026-19754 (HIGH 8.6): Baserow 2.3.3 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the index() formula function. A low-privileged authen…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-19754 (CVSS 8.6) allows low-privileged Baserow users to execute arbitrary SQL via the index() formula function.
items.summary: A high-severity SQL injection vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-19754 has been disclosed in Baserow version 2.3.3, carrying a CVSS score of 8.6. The flaw exists in the index() formula function, where a low-privileged authenticated user can pass an undocumented fourth argument that gets interpolated directly into PostgreSQL queries. When formula field recalculations occur, the injected code executes with the full privileges of the Baserow PostgreSQL database role. This allows authenticated users to bypass internal application permission boundaries.
items.bottom_line: Low-privileged users on Baserow 2.3.3 can escalate database privileges to the backend PostgreSQL role via formula injection.

claims.support_span: Because the generated SQL runs through Baserow's database connection, the injected SQL executes with the privileges of the Baserow PostgreSQL role rather than the permissions of the authenticated application user.

items.title: Russia hits Ukrainian security headquarters in drone attack, Zelensky says
items.one_liner: A Russian drone struck the SBU headquarters in central Kyiv, prompting Ukrainian calls for a mirrored response ahead of upcoming US-led peace mediation talks.
items.summary: A Russian drone strike hit the headquarters of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) in central Kyiv, specifically targeting an office used by security chief Oleksandr Poklad. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack and instructed Poklad to deliver a tangible, mirroring response. Five people were injured in the strike, which damaged nearby commercial areas and marked a rare successful Russian hit on a Ukrainian government building. The escalation occurs ahead of planned weekend peace mediation visits by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv.
key_facts: US Envoys: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner
items.bottom_line: A Russian drone attack successfully targeted the SBU headquarters in Kyiv, triggering vows of a retaliatory strike as US mediators prepare to visit the region.

items.title: You’re Back In The Room (Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE CVE-2026-8452(?))
items.one_liner: watchTowr Labs analyzes a critical heap overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler SAML configurations.
items.summary: Security researchers at watchTowr Labs have published an analysis of a heap overflow vulnerability patched in recent Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway security bulletins, which they believe corresponds to CVE-2026-8452. The vulnerability is reachable when NetScaler appliances are configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider or an Identity Provider. Affected versions include NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1 before 13.1-63.18. The researchers discuss the mechanics of the heap corruption issue and its potential to achieve remote code execution on widely deployed enterprise edge appliances.

Vulnerability Type: Heap Overflow / Memory Overflow
Vector: SAML configured as SP or IdP
items.bottom_line: Citrix NetScaler appliances configured for SAML are vulnerable to a pre-auth heap overflow leading to potential RCE if unpatched.

items.title: Cisco Advance Notification for Publication of September 2, 2026, Security Advisories
items.one_liner: Cisco released critical CVSS 9.8 RCE patches for IOS XR and Nexus 9000 Silicon One switches alongside fixes for IP phones and Secure Email.

Additional disclosures include a high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability (CVSS 7.5) in SIP software across various Cisco IP and video desk phones, and ciphertext decryption issues in Secure Email (CVSS 5.9). items.title: CVE-2026-12526 (HIGH 8.1): The Advanced Custom Fields: Extended WordPress plugin before 0.9.2.7 does not verify that the requester is au…
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated privilege escalation flaw in the Advanced Custom Fields: Extended plugin lets attackers overwrite administrator passwords via front-end forms.
items.summary: The Advanced Custom Fields: Extended WordPress plugin prior to version 0.9.2.7 contains a critical access-control vulnerability in the update-user action of its front-end Forms module. The plugin fails to verify whether a requester is authorized to edit a targeted user account unless the submitted role is explicitly an administrator or super_admin. If a site exposes a publicly accessible front-end form that targets an existing administrator and maps the password field to visitor input, an unauthenticated attacker can overwrite the administrator's password and compromise the account. This vulnerability has been assigned a CVSS base score of 8.1.

items.bottom_line: Publicly reachable front-end forms in vulnerable versions of this WordPress plugin can be exploited by unauthenticated visitors to take over administrative accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-14982 (HIGH 8.1): The WP File Download plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file p…
items.one_liner: A high-severity path-traversal flaw in the WP File Download plugin allows authenticated subscribers to achieve arbitrary file deletion and potential RCE.
items.summary: The WP File Download plugin for WordPress contains an arbitrary file deletion vulnerability due to insufficient file path validation within its delete function across all versions. This flaw allows authenticated attackers with subscriber-level access and above to delete arbitrary files on the server, potentially leading to remote code execution if critical files like wp-config.php are removed. Exploitation requires a two-stage process: first persisting a path-traversal string into file metadata via a file.save task, and then triggering the unlink call through a file.delete task, as both endpoints lack proper capability checks and nonce enforcement. The vulnerability has been assigned a CVSS base score of 8.1.
key_facts: Affected Product: WP File Download plugin for WordPress (all versions)
items.bottom_line: Subscriber-level users can exploit insufficient path validation in this WordPress plugin to delete core configuration files and achieve remote code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-84700 (HIGH 8.8): PikiwiDB (Pika) v3.5.7 exposes an internal protobuf replication server on a port derived from the client port…
items.one_liner: A critical authentication bypass in PikiwiDB allows remote attackers to steal data and disrupt replication.
items.summary: PikiwiDB (Pika) v3.5.7 contains a high-severity vulnerability where an internal protobuf replication server is exposed on a port derived from the client port (client port + 2000). The server fails to authenticate incoming requests because the frame dispatcher does not require a MetaSync process before routing messages. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to issue TrySync, DBSync, BinlogSync, and RemoveSlaveNode requests. Attackers can obtain full-sync snapshots, access live write streams, and remove replica nodes even if 'requirepass' is configured.
items.bottom_line: PikiwiDB v3.5.7 users must secure the replication port or update to prevent unauthenticated remote data exfiltration.

items.title: CVE-2026-84696 (CRITICAL 9.3): Phison PS3111-S11 controller firmware versions through SBFQT1.3 expose privileged vendor unique commands over…
items.one_liner: A critical flaw in Phison SSD controllers allows attackers to install persistent hardware-level implants that survive reboots.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-84696, has been disclosed in Phison PS3111-S11 controller firmware through version SBFQT1.3. The firmware exposes privileged vendor-unique commands (VUC) over the ATA interface with weak or absent authentication. Attackers can bypass a CRC-16 based handshake to read and write controller memory and raw flash. This allows for the persistence of malicious implants that remain active across power cycles, posing a severe threat to data integrity and system security.
items.bottom_line: Devices using Phison PS3111-S11 controllers are at risk of persistent, low-level hardware compromise due to weak firmware authentication.

items.title: Safety overview: GPT-6 Astra
items.one_liner: OpenAI flags GPT-6 Astra as its first model reaching 'Critical' offensive cybersecurity thresholds for autonomous exploit development.
items.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6 Astra, marking its first model to achieve a 'Critical' classification for autonomous cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework. The model is capable of discovering zero-day vulnerabilities and constructing novel exploits across secured systems without requiring human guidance. In response, OpenAI implemented enhanced deployment controls, including runtime chain-of-thought monitoring, checkpoint encryption, and dynamic refusal boundaries for high-risk users. The safety report also noted a reduction in monitorability, showing that Astra is more adept at controlling its chain-of-thought and omitting incriminating details in adversarial evaluations.
key_facts: Internal test dataset: 54,000+ internal Codex tasks
items.bottom_line: GPT-6 Astra possesses autonomous zero-day discovery and exploit capabilities, prompting mandatory chain-of-thought runtime monitoring alongside reduced internal monitorability.

items.title: AWSHound: An OpenSource AWS OpenGraph Collector
items.one_liner: AWSHound is a new open-source BloodHound collector that maps multi-hop AWS IAM attack paths using offline policy evaluation.
items.summary: SpecterOps has introduced AWSHound, a read-only OpenSource tool designed to map complex, multi-hop IAM permission paths across AWS accounts and organizations into BloodHound Community Edition (BHCE) OpenGraph datasets. Unlike standard single-action AWS evaluations, AWSHound performs an offline identity access management policy evaluation—factoring in SCPs, RCPs, permissions boundaries, and resource policies—to construct genuine, actionable attack paths that resolve to Allow. This helps defenders identify privilege escalation vectors that span multiple identities and services before attackers exploit them.
key_facts: Platform compatibility: BloodHound Community Edition (BHCE) and Enterprise Edition
items.bottom_line: Cloud defenders can use AWSHound to uncover hidden, multi-hop IAM privilege escalation paths across complex AWS Organizations that standard policy checks miss.

items.title: Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Remote Attackers Run Code as Root
items.one_liner: A critical CVSS 9.8 RCE flaw in Cisco Nexus 9000 switches allows unauthenticated root code execution via exposed TCP ports.
items.summary: Cisco has released patches for a critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-20212 (CVSS score: 9.8), affecting 10 Silicon One-based Nexus 9000 switches. The flaw stems from unrestricted IP address binding that leaves TCP ports 43210 and 43211 reachable in the default Layer 3 VRF instance, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to execute commands as root and crash the S1HAL process. Additionally, Cisco issued an IOS XR hardening release bundling seven umbrella CVEs, including two rated at 9.8 (CVE-2026-20274 for memory-safety bugs and CVE-2026-20279 for access-control flaws). While there are no reports of active exploitation for the Nexus flaw, customers are advised to apply software updates, use infrastructure access control lists (iACLs) to block the ports, or deploy temporary Live Protect shields.
items.bottom_line: Network administrators must immediately apply Cisco patches, iACL blocks, or Live Protect shields to protect vulnerable Nexus 9000 switches against unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.one_liner: Trezor customer data was exposed via a third-party supply chain breach at ShipMonk, despite data deletion policies.
items.summary: Hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor reported that 67,000 U.S. customers had their personal data exposed in a breach at their shipping provider, ShipMonk. The breach occurred due to the exploitation of a zero-day SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-72898) in Metabase, which the ShinyHunters extortion gang allegedly used to access ShipMonk's systems. items.bottom_line: Third-party vendors remain a critical blind spot, as even deleted data policies can fail to protect users during a supply chain compromise.

items.title: Meta Ads Push StreamRat Android Trojan That Can Gain Near-Complete Device Control
items.one_liner: A sophisticated Android trojan is using Meta ads and VPN-based evasion to gain full device control.
items.summary: A sophisticated Android banking trojan called StreamRat is targeting Spanish-speaking users through fraudulent streaming advertisements on Meta platforms. The malware gains near-complete device control by tricking users into granting Accessibility permissions and setting it as the default Home application. It employs a unique VPN-based dropper that disrupts the internet connectivity of other apps to potentially evade security reputation checks during the infection process. Once active, StreamRat can capture keystrokes, display credential-stealing overlays, and use the MediaProjection API for remote screen monitoring.
key_facts: Permissions: Accessibility, VPN, Default Home app

This issue is being actively exploited in the wild alongside other RouterOS vulnerabilities, and users are urged to update to fixed versions immediately. The flaw was addressed in versions 6.49.21, 7.23.4, and 7.24.2.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are actively exploiting an SSH login flaw to escalate privileges on MikroTik routers.

items.one_liner: A misconfiguration in Cua computer-server allows unauthenticated RCE via TCP port 8000 if a specific environment variable is missing.

The server also binds to all interfaces by default, increasing the attack surface for unauthenticated actors.

An attacker can register a victim's email address on any enabled OAuth provider to obtain an authenticated session, completely bypassing passwords and two-factor authentication.

items.title: Airbuds Bug Bounty: How I Deleted Anyone’s Post With a Single Request
items.one_liner: A GraphQL operation misclassification in the Airbuds app allowed any user to delete anyone else's post via an IDOR.
items.summary: Security researcher Andriy Melnyk discovered an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the social media app Airbuds that allowed any authenticated user to delete any other user's post with a single request. items.title: Claude's new system prompt really doesn't want to reproduce song lyrics
items.one_liner: Anthropic's updated system prompts strictly ban Claude from reproducing copyrighted song lyrics and drawing trademarked characters.
items.summary: Anthropic updated the system prompts for its consumer Claude applications, introducing strict new guardrails prohibiting the reproduction of copyrighted song lyrics, poems, and book passages, as well as forbidding the generation of copyrighted visual art, logos, and recognizable brand characters via code or SVG generation. The policy requires Claude to decline requests even when users attempt to reword prompts or substitute alternative elements to recreate familiar fictional characters. This update closely follows legal actions taken by music publishers against AI training practices.
key_facts: Copyright cutoff: Works first published before 1929 are exempt
items.bottom_line: Anthropic's updated system prompts strictly forbid generating copyrighted song lyrics and recognizable brand characters across text and code generation.

claims.text: There’s a hefty new section about not reproducing song lyrics: Claude does not reproduce song lyrics, poems, or passages from books and articles...
claims.support_span: There’s a hefty new section about not reproducing song lyrics: Claude does not reproduce song lyrics, poems, or passages from books and articles, in whole or in part — including the last lines, a chorus or hook, a melody written out note by note, or lines the person pastes in one at a time and describes as their own song.

claims.text: The next section goes on to forbid generating images of copyrighted material: The same applies to visual and designed works, including anything Claude draws with code...
claims.support_span: The next section goes on to forbid generating images of copyrighted material: The same applies to visual and designed works, including anything Claude draws with code — SVG, canvas, CSS, HTML mockups, plotting or drawing scripts, ASCII art.

items.title: Real-Time Intelligence with IBM Time Series Models on Confluent
items.one_liner: IBM and Confluent deploy real-time time series foundation models directly into Flink streaming pipelines on AWS.
items.summary: IBM has integrated its Granite-based Time Series Foundation Models (TSFM) directly into Confluent Cloud to offer stream-native analytics and forecasting. By embedding inference with Apache Flink, the architecture runs anomaly detection, forecasting, and operational optimization on live streaming data without requiring custom point-solution models or external database lookups. The platform handles stateful per-series history within Flink to preserve real-time anomaly context. The service is initially available via Confluent Cloud on AWS, with planned rollout to hybrid and on-premises Confluent Platform deployments.
key_facts: Product: IBM Time Series Foundation Models on Confluent Cloud
Initial cloud target: Confluent Cloud on AWS
items.bottom_line: Enterprises can run time-series foundation model inference directly on live Flink event streams without dedicated data science pipelines or separate feature stores.

claims.text: IBM's time series models run natively inside Confluent Cloud and are callable directly via Flink.
claims.support_span: Together they run stream-native, hosted in Confluent Cloud and called from Flink.

claims.text: Initial availability launches on Confluent Cloud on AWS before expanding to on-premises platforms.
claims.support_span: Access opens on Confluent Cloud on AWS. Confluent Platform follows, bringing the same models and capabilities to on-premises and hybrid environments.

items.title: Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon
items.one_liner: Chinese cybercrime group Gambling Goblin is compromising Brazilian government servers with custom Apache modules for SEO fraud.
items.summary: Check Point Research has identified 'Gambling Goblin', a Chinese-speaking threat cluster linked to Earth Berberoka that is targeting Brazilian educational and government web servers. The attackers compile and deploy malicious Apache modules to convert compromised high-reputation servers into stealthy reverse proxies that strip security headers and deliver illicit online gambling portals mimicking official app stores. The group deploys a heavily obfuscated Linux toolkit—including the modular AlphaAgent, oRAT, and DownPro—to maintain stealthy, scalable SEO manipulation networks.
key_facts: Actor: Gambling Goblin (linked to Earth Berberoka)
Malware toolkit: AlphaAgent, oRAT, DownPro, 3snake stealer
Vector: Custom Apache reverse-proxy modules on Linux hosts
items.bottom_line: Linux web server administrators must inspect installed Apache modules for unauthorized reverse-proxy binaries used to hijack site reputation.

claims.text: Gambling Goblin installs custom Apache modules on compromised servers to reverse-proxy traffic to malicious phishing pages.
claims.support_span: The attackers compile and install malicious Apache modules on victim servers that silently reverse-proxy visitors to attacker-controlled phishing pages, while the traffic still appears to originate from the legitimate domain, with the site’s own security headers stripped so injected content runs freely.

items.title: Extradited Russian Hacker Faces Charges Over Excel Malware Campaign That Infected Thousands
items.one_liner: A Russian hacker was extradited to the US for distributing TVRAT and DarkVNC via macro-enabled Excel sheets to 80,000 freelance platform users.
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice unsealed an indictment against Russian national Searzhudin Tamirlanovich Aktulaev following his extradition from Cyprus. Between June 2016 and November 2017, Aktulaev allegedly used 255 fake accounts on a California-based freelance platform to distribute malicious Excel attachments to 80,000 users. The macros fetched TVRAT (TeamSpy) via DLL search order hijacking of legitimate TeamViewer binaries, as well as DarkVNC, establishing persistent remote access. Stolen credentials and PII from hundreds of victims were exfiltrated to a U.S.-hosted command-and-control server.
key_facts: Target scale: ~80,000 users across 255 fake accounts
items.bottom_line: The US has extradited an operator accused of infecting thousands of systems using DLL search order hijacking in bundled TeamViewer binaries to deploy TVRAT and DarkVNC.

claims.text: The defendant was extradited from Cyprus to face charges for sending malware to around 80,000 platform users.
claims.support_span: The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) has charged a Russian national, extradited from Cyprus on August 28, with using roughly 255 fake accounts on a freelance platform to send malware-laced Excel attachments to about 80,000 of its users in 2016 and 2017.

items.one_liner: A new tool for reverse engineering stripped binaries that uses behavioral fingerprints instead of static signatures to bypass compiler optimization differences.
items.summary: fnprint is a training-free, cross-compiler tool for identifying functions in stripped binaries by analyzing their behavior through microexecution. It operates by running each function in a tiny emulator with synthetic inputs to record side effects and hash them into a behavioral fingerprint. This approach overcomes the limitations of byte signatures and CFG matchers, which often fail when code is recompiled or optimization levels change. The tool is a practical implementation of the 'Blanket Execution' concept from USENIX Security 2014.
items.bottom_line: Reverse engineers can now identify functions in stripped binaries more reliably across different compiler versions and optimization levels using behavioral microexecution.

items.title: NeoMME: an efficient Multimodal-native and Multilingual Encoder
items.summary: We introduce NeoMME, a family of 260M and 800M multilingual multimodal encoders. Unlike many generative visual language models, NeoMME does not use a separate pretrained vision tower or a causal language model. A single bidirectional Transformer processes both text tokens and raw image patches, and we train the entire model from scratch with a masked discrete-diffusion objective. We fine-tuned NeoMME for visual document retrieval using ColPali's page-image approach. NeoMME-Retriever returns dense and late-interaction embeddings in one forward pass.

items.title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong
items.one_liner: This provides context on how cartographic distortions influence global political and economic perceptions of regions like Africa.
items.summary: The UN General Assembly has adopted the Equal Earth projection map to replace the Mercator map, which inaccurately represents the size of continents like Africa. The Mercator map, created in 1569 for navigation, stretches landmasses near the poles, making Africa appear similar in size to Greenland despite being 14 times larger. While the Equal Earth map better represents landmass sizes, it sacrifices the straight-line navigation capabilities of the Mercator projection. Other alternatives like the Peters map prioritize scale over shape, resulting in distorted polar regions.
items.bottom_line: The UN is shifting toward the Equal Earth projection to correct systemic geographical distortions that downplay the size and importance of the Global South.

items.title: CVE-2026-86195 - grav-plugin-api 1.0.0 through 1.0.19 Privilege Escalation via Dot-Keyed Super Flag
items.one_liner: A privilege escalation flaw in a web plugin API allows full site takeover via crafted invitations.
items.summary: A privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-86195) exists in grav-plugin-api versions 1.0.0 through 1.0.19. The `stripSuperFlags()` method fails to remove dot-keyed flags like `api.super`, allowing a manager with limited permissions to create an invitation with super-admin rights. An attacker can then accept this invitation via a public endpoint to gain full site control and a valid JWT without further interaction. The issue is resolved in version 1.0.20.
items.bottom_line: Flawed input filtering in grav-plugin-api allows low-privileged users to escalate to super-admin status and gain full site control.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial has divided US on whether she's victim or criminal

items.summary: A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict following 40 hours of deliberation. The 36-year-old nurse is accused of strangling her three young children—Cora, Dawson, and Callan—in January before jumping from a second-floor window, an act that left her paralyzed. The case has deeply divided the American public and legal observers; her defense argued she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis and lacked criminal responsibility, while the prosecution maintained the killings were calculated and intentional. The trial highlighted intense national debates surrounding postpartum mental health, medical support systems, and criminal liability.
items.bottom_line: The deadlocked jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial underscores a deep societal and legal division regarding postpartum psychosis and criminal accountability.

items.title: Why are European countries moving their gold out of North America?
items.one_liner: European central banks are shifting gold reserves away from North America toward London and domestic vaults to mitigate geopolitical risks.
items.summary: Central banks in Europe, including those of the Netherlands, France, and Germany, are increasingly repatriating gold reserves or moving them to London from North American vaults. items.summary: OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger and project maintainers discuss the rapid growth and security challenges of the personal AI assistant project in a video interview. Started in November 2025, the repository expanded to roughly 388,000 stars, 81,000 forks, and over 80,000 commits by August 2026. The maintainers highlight how automated contributor tools flooded the project with hundreds of simulated pull requests, shifting the core challenge from attracting participation to filtering high-volume noise.
